description: A premium tower event planning tool at /analyze/tower-planner that auto-detects active tower events, shows per-room requirements, calculates roster readiness, runs a constraint solver to auto-assign optimal teams, auto-detects progress from the API, recommends upgrades, tracks historical performance, and sends push notifications. Full E2E and unit test coverage required.

userStories.title: Tower API route — fetch active tower events and layout
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need a backend API route that detects the active tower event and returns its layout so that the frontend can display tower structure.
acceptanceCriteria: New API route at src/app/api/tower/events/route.ts
GET handler fetches /game/v1/events?eventInfo=full&perPage=100 via msfApiFetch and filters for type 'pickYourPoison' with tower-related naming
Cross-references with /game/v1/survivalTowers to get tower layout (rays, rooms)
Returns JSON: { active: boolean, tower: { id, name, endDate, currentWeek, rays: [{ id, rooms: [{ id, name }] }] } | null }
currentWeek calculated from event startTime (week 1 = first 7 days, week 2 = after)
Returns { active: false, tower: null } when no tower event found
Unit test in src/app/api/tower/events/route.test.ts verifies: correct tower detection from mock events, correct week calculation, empty response when no tower active
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Foundation route. All other stories depend on tower detection working. Uses existing msfApiFetch from src/lib/msf-api.ts.

userStories.title: Tower API route — per-room requirements with player auth
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need to fetch per-room trait/gear/star requirements using the player's auth token so that readiness can be calculated.
acceptanceCriteria: New API route at src/app/api/tower/rooms/route.ts
GET handler accepts query param towerId, fetches /player/v1/survivalTowers/{towerId} using user's session token
Returns JSON array of rooms: [{ id, rayId, name, requirements: { traits: string[], minGearTier: number, minStars: number, minLevel: number }, week: 1|2 }]
Rooms ordered by ray (A first, then B, then C) and room number within each ray
Returns 401 if user is not authenticated
Returns 404 if towerId not found or API returns error
Unit test in src/app/api/tower/rooms/route.test.ts verifies: correct auth passing, room ordering, 401 for unauthed, 404 for bad tower ID
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 for tower ID. The player endpoint requires user auth — use getServerSession to get token.

userStories.title: Tower readiness calculation library
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need a library that compares player roster against room requirements to determine readiness status per room.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/lib/tower-readiness.ts exports calculateRoomReadiness(roster, roomRequirements) and calculateOverallReadiness(roomStatuses)
calculateRoomReadiness returns: { status: 'ready'|'almost'|'blocked', eligibleCount: number, eligibleCharacters: Character[] }
Status logic: 'ready' = 5+ chars meeting ALL thresholds (traits + gear + stars + level), 'almost' = 3-4 eligible or 5 with some below one threshold, 'blocked' = fewer than 3 eligible
calculateOverallReadiness returns: { readyCount, almostCount, blockedCount, totalRooms, summary: string }
summary is plain English like 'You can likely clear 10 of 12 battles this tower'
Unit test in src/lib/tower-readiness.test.ts with test fixtures covering: all-ready roster, mixed roster, severely-blocked roster, edge case of exactly 5 with one below gear
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Pure logic library — no API calls, no UI. Roster comes from existing RosterSnapshot model. Room requirements come from US-002 API.

userStories.title: Tower constraint solver — team allocation algorithm
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need a constraint solver that optimally distributes teams across all rooms to maximize clearable rooms without wasting strong characters on easy battles.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/lib/tower-solver.ts exports solveTowerAllocation(rooms, roster, metaTeams, clearedRooms?)
Returns: { assignments: Map<roomId, { characters: Character[], power: number, confidence: 'strong'|'shouldWork'|'risky', reason: string }>, unassignableRooms: string[] }
Solver allocates globally (not greedy room-by-room) — assigns weakest viable team to each room, preserving strong characters for harder rooms
Respects cooldown: each character assigned to at most one room per week
Respects all room requirements: traits, gear tier, stars, level
When power levels are within 10%, prefers meta team compositions from teamOrder/tower data
confidence: 'strong' when team power exceeds estimated need by 20%+, 'shouldWork' for 0-20% margin, 'risky' when barely meeting minimums
reason: 1-2 sentence explanation (e.g., 'Your strongest Mutant team — 150k above minimum')
Handles edge cases: rooms with no valid team get added to unassignableRooms, already-cleared rooms are skipped

Unit test in src/lib/tower-solver.test.ts: solver doesn't double-assign characters, respects trait requirements, assigns weaker teams to easy rooms, handles no-solution gracefully, excludes cleared rooms
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: This is the core algorithm. No UI, no API calls — pure function. Takes pre-fetched data. Meta teams come from /game/v1/analysis/teamOrder/tower (fetched elsewhere).

userStories.title: Tower upgrade recommendations library
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need logic that identifies which character upgrades would unlock the most additional rooms so players know what to farm.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/lib/tower-upgrades.ts exports getUpgradeRecommendations(rooms, roster, readinessResults)
Returns: Array<{ characterName, currentValue, targetValue, upgradeType: 'gear'|'stars'|'level', roomsUnlocked: string[], impact: number }> sorted by impact descending
For 'almost' rooms: identifies the specific gap (e.g., character at G16 needs G17)
For 'blocked' rooms: explains why (e.g., 'Requires Storm (Mighty) — unlocked from this tower')
Maximum 5 recommendations returned (highest impact first)
impact = number of additional rooms that upgrade would unlock
Unit test in src/lib/tower-upgrades.test.ts: correct gap identification, sorted by impact, max 5 cap, blocked rooms get explanation
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Pure logic. Depends on readiness results from US-003. No UI.

userStories.title: Tower meta teams API route
userStories.description: As the tower planner, I need to fetch tower meta team data so the solver can prefer proven compositions.
acceptanceCriteria: New API route at src/app/api/tower/meta-teams/route.ts
GET handler fetches /game/v1/analysis/teamOrder/tower?perPage=200 via msfApiFetch
Returns JSON: { teams: [{ squad: string[], usageTotal: number, winRate?: number }] }
squad contains character IDs that map to existing character data
Unit test in src/app/api/tower/meta-teams/route.test.ts verifies correct response shape and pass-through
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Simple pass-through API route. Uses client credentials (no user auth needed).

userStories.title: TowerResult database model for history tracking
userStories.description: As the system, I need a database table to store tower event results so players can see their performance history.
acceptanceCriteria: New Prisma model TowerResult with fields: id (cuid), userId (relation to User), towerEventId (string), towerName (string), roomsCleared (int), totalRooms (int), week1Cleared (int), week2Cleared (int), completedAt (DateTime)
Compound unique constraint on [userId, towerEventId] (one result per user per tower event)
prisma migrate dev creates the migration successfully
New API route at src/app/api/tower/history/route.ts — GET returns user's past results sorted by completedAt desc
POST to same route creates/updates a TowerResult record
Unit tests verify: GET returns empty array for new user, POST creates record, duplicate towerEventId upserts
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Schema-first story. Must complete before UI can display history.
